eval: Many species of cephalopods are known for their ability to change color and texture for camouflage.
These marine animals can escape from enclosures by squeezing through small openings due to their soft bodies.
In some coastal regions, they exhibit problem-solving skills by manipulating objects to obtain food.
Individuals often use ink as a defense mechanism to confuse predators and facilitate escape.
They are known to inhabit diverse environments, ranging from coral reefs to deep ocean floors.
Some species display social behaviors, engaging in complex interactions with others of their kind.
A diet primarily consists of crustaceans and small fish that they capture using specialized appendages.
Reproductive strategies can include laying thousands of eggs in hidden locations to protect them from predators.
train: This marine creature has eight long, flexible arms covered in small suction cups.
The body of this animal is soft and can change shape to fit through tight spaces.
Color-changing abilities are facilitated by specialized cells in the skin called chromatophores.
A large brain is located in the head, which is highly developed compared to other invertebrates.
This animal possesses a beak-like mouth that can efficiently break through hard shells.
The arms contain a network of neurons, allowing for complex movements and coordination.
These creatures have a unique method of locomotion, using a form of jet propulsion to swim.
The skin can produce a thick ink that is released as a defense mechanism against predators.
